Outcome_variable.extract_value: life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect
Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/12] Well-being. As in previous research (e.g., Sheldon et al., 2004; Sheldon & Kasser, 1995), we included life satisfaction and affect as indicators of subjective well-being. Life satisfaction was measured with the five-item Satisfaction With Life Scale (Diener, Emmons, Larsen, & Griffin, 1985; α = .85), answered on a 7-point Likert-type scale anchored at 1 = not at all and 7 = completely. [/page/3/Text/13] Affect was measured with the subscales Positive Emotions and Negative Activation from the short version [/page/4/Text/5] of the Multidimensional Mood Questionnaire (Steyer, Schwenkmezger, Notz, & Eid, 1997).
